precepts.text: And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King! But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar. Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away. That is how he was taken from prison and from judgment.
precepts.point: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken. Now, we might think that Christ does not understand what we are going through. I am going to show you that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, but I want to focus on verse 8. He was taken from prison and from judgment. He was cut off out of the land of the living: that is when he was crucified.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
We might think that Christ doesn't understand what we are going through. Isaiah 53 shows that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, and verse 8 says: “He was taken from prison and from judgment.” How?

John shows it. “And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend.” Pilate “brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.”

“And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King! But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar. Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.”

That is how he was taken from prison and from judgment: bound, set before the judgment seat, rejected by his own for Caesar, and led away. The one who was taken from prison is the one who comes to preach to our people, who are in the prison house today.

precepts.text: The soldiers brake the legs of the two crucified with him, but when they came to Jesus and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: thus fulfilling the prophecy of Psalms 34:20.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
This is the fulfilment. “The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken”.

“Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs”.

They broke the legs of the two crucified with him, but not his. Thus fulfilling the prophecy in Psalms 34:20, and the passover command, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Christ was that passover lamb, and there is still more meat to scrape off the bones of this.

precepts.why:
“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil, from the white man's lies, Christianity, Judaism and all that foolishness, you become a target, a prey to the red dragon, the Jewish community and the American government. That is what Christ said this walk is about. So to the celebrities and influential brothers and sisters who watch, Nick Cannon and all of you: don't run out and tell your Jewish friends you are a Black Hebrew Israelite. Reach out, build yourself up, learn how to fight first, and seek counsel from the leaders on how you can be used in this war.

John shows how our people who are rich and famous have to follow this truth: “And after this Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly.” He was a secret follower. He did not put himself out in front; he supported behind the scenes, and that is better.

Remember Kyrie Irving. He didn't announce he was with any group. He sent one tweet, and they annihilated him, fined him, and made him go back and apologize. Ye went and apologized the other day, and now he is back to 250 million dollar tours. The problem with a lot of our people is that we love social media. You tweet your whole life and tell everybody everything, and Christ never said to do that. When he entered a city he would have no man know it, though he could not be hid. Put your whole life out there and it will cost you in the end.

Daddy’s home. That is the Daddy in the scriptures. The chief priests rejected their own King and claimed Caesar, just as our people today reject the truth and call the white man daddy.

Then they act confused when he shows his true colors and rolls back DEI. You knew it was a snake. That is what Christianity does: you never read the Bible, you are put to sleep every week, and when you go out in the world everybody sees color except you. Open your Bible. Never trust thine enemy.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
The rulers who said “were never in bondage to any man” show whose servants they really were. Pilate “saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!” “But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him.” Kill him. “Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.”

Our king is the white man; that's our leader. That is what the chief priests confessed: Caesar was their king. Today it's the same: our king is the joint chiefs of America, Caesar Borgia, Pope Nicholas V. Like the born and bred slaves in 12 Years a Slave who keep their heads down and call out to master, they have no fight in them and lay in the white man's bosom.

“And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.” The Herodians were a Jewish political faction who supported the Herodian dynasty, aligning with Roman rule for political stability. Herod was an Idumean, the same Edomites the Maccabees fought against, set up as Edomite kings over us, and these Jews aligned with them and with the Romans ruling over us.

We have our people today who desire and fight for the white man to reign over us by any means necessary: the Herodians of today, the black commentators and content creators who defend Trump, cry over Charlie Kirk, speak evil of their own people, and worship money and the power the white man gives them. They are financial idolaters. All skinfolk ain't kinfolk.

precepts.text: These things were done that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken; Christ is the Passover lamb.
precepts.point: Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
“In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.” Not a bone of the Passover lamb was to be broken. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb.

On the cross his bones were not broken, and John says why: “For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.” The scripture being fulfilled is this ordinance of the passover. What was commanded of the lamb in Egypt was kept in the body of Christ, because he is the lamb the ordinance was about.

precepts.text: The title on the cross was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, the languages of the captivities Israel was placed under.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Pilate's title on the cross shows the tongues in Jerusalem itself: “JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. This title then read many of the Jews”, and “it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin.”

Those are the languages of the captivities Israel was placed under, and many of the Jews read them. Israel had been placed under those captivities, which is why the word had to go to them in those languages. So when the cloven tongues sat on the apostles, they were divided into the languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, the very languages written over Christ's head.

note.label: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

precepts.why:
Who’s the king Israel was delivered into the hand of? “Whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cesar.” Pilate “saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!” “But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.”

We have no king but Caesar. Our people loved Rome, and the chief priests loved Rome, because Rome gave them wealth, Rome gave them position, Rome gave them authority. So Christ’s crime was treason, for being king. That’s why Pilate kept mocking him, shall I crucify your king, and that’s what was on the cross. So when Zechariah says “into the hand of his king”, the king is Caesar.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away. And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha”.

They led him out of the city. And what was he carrying? The cross: the wood. The bullock was burnt on the wood without the camp, and Christ bore the wood and suffered without the gate.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why: How do we know came by water and blood means that? “But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.” That shows he came in the fleshly form.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: Apollos Creed

precepts.why:
“When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.” The Jews besought Pilate “that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.” “Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him”: there were two other brothers crucified with Christ. “But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.”

“For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.” That is the scripture we just read in Psalms, and there is one in the book of Numbers as well, to show that even from way back in the time of Moses this was already being prophesied.

This is how these brothers broke it down; this is how they knew Christ was Christ. Some of the brothers walking with Christ weren’t even 100% believing: you have the brother named Thomas. The disciples went to the gravesite to anoint his body, although he told them he would be gone; they weren’t thinking it was actually going to happen. It wasn’t that Christ talked to them and they understood it right away. They learned over time, and they had to have faith.

note.label: From Desolation to Dominion

precepts.why: “Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him”: they beat Jesus. “The soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe, and said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.” They put a purple robe on Christ and started punching him in the face, smacking him upside the head: the judge of Israel smitten upon the cheek.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
Why they always said John was the one Christ loved. Remember Peter denied Christ; when he was on the cross everybody deserted Christ. But watch this. “Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved,” This is John. “he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!” So Christ said to his mother to look at John: behold your son, he's going to take care of you now.

“Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother!” John was the only one there; everybody else took off running, John stuck by Christ. So now he says to John, behold your mother, meaning my mother is now your mother. “And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.” That's why the scriptures always made reference to John whom Christ loved. They all loved Christ, don't get me wrong, but John was on another level of love and admiration and dedication and loyalty.

note.label: Unlocking The Three Angels Prophecies And More

Caesar is also pronounced Kaiser, Khazar: it’s the same word.
